children: The WASDE's partial offset of reductions made to the amount of wheat Russia is expected to export this marketing year weighed on CBOT futures after the report's release. Russian exports were cut by 3 million metric tons to 40 million tons. But those cuts were partially offset by gains of half-a-million tons each for Argentina and Canada. This, along with the USDA projecting a slightly larger wheat crop in the U.S. this year sent CBOT wheat futures lower. The most-active contract falls 1.8%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
